title: British Overseas Territories
capsule: The British Overseas Territories (BOTs) are 14 jurisdictions that retain a formal link to the United Kingdom following the British Overseas Territories Act 2002, which also granted full British citizenship to their inhabitants — reversing the exclusions of the British Nationality Act 1981. The territories include strategically significant sites such as Gibraltar, the Falkland Islands, Diego Garcia (British Indian Ocean Territory), Akrotiri and Dhekelia (Cyprus), and Bermuda, as well as remote possessions like South Georgia and the British Antarctic Territory. Each territory has its own government and legal system; the UK retains responsibility for defense and foreign affairs, and the relationship with each territory differs in degree of self-governance.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. As a collective category rather than a single polity, territorial extent cannot be represented by a single polygon; each constituent territory has precisely mapped boundaries, though several (Falklands, Gibraltar, British Antarctic Territory) are subject to sovereignty disputes.
